title: Degrees of Certainty About the Past

sections.title: How Sure Were We?
sections.content: You know how to rate certainty from B1 Unit 22 and earlier units: *biztosan* ('surely'), *valószínűleg* ('probably'), *talán* ('perhaps'), *Lehet, hogy* ... ('It may be that ...') and *Kétlem, hogy* ... ('I doubt that ...'). Here you use them with the past tense to judge what people knew in a case: 'Valószínűleg tudta, hogy veszélyes.' (He probably knew it was dangerous.) 'Talán észrevette a jeleket.' (Perhaps he noticed the signs.)

sections.title: Doubt and Missed Chances
sections.content: After *Kétlem, hogy* the verb stays in the indicative past: 'Kétlem, hogy tudta.' (I doubt that he knew.) When the point is a chance that was missed, use *kellett volna* or *lehetett volna* (B1 Unit 20): 'Észre kellett volna venni a jeleket.' (The signs should have been noticed.) 'Hamarabb fel lehetett volna ismerni a bajt.' (The trouble could have been recognized sooner.)

sections.title: Certainty About the Past
rows: He surely knew that it was dangerous.
It may be that he did not know about it.

items.spanish: Valószínűleg tudta, hogy a betegség veszélyes.
items.english: He probably knew that the illness was dangerous.

items.spanish: Kétlem, hogy az orvosok észrevették a jeleket.
items.english: I doubt that the doctors noticed the signs.

items.spanish: A jeleket hamarabb fel kellett volna ismerni.
items.english: The signs should have been recognized sooner.

sections.title: B2 Stylistic Notice
sections.content: *Biztosan*, *valószínűleg* and *talán* stand before the verb or the focus word and do not change the verb form. Use *kellett volna* / *lehetett volna* only for a missed chance, not for guessing.
